candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies client-needs subcategory (13–19% of items); this item tests recognition and prevention of medication-related hypotension during therapy adjustment.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Medication adverse-effect monitoring and dose-titration safety for antispastic therapy
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients taking tizanidine to recognize hypotension and orthostatic symptoms during titration and ensure these effects are assessed before dosage increases.

options.A: Monitor for dizziness, lightheadedness, or other signs of hypotension, especially before the dose is increased
options.B: Expect tizanidine to raise blood pressure, so hypotension monitoring is unnecessary
options.C: Ignore orthostatic symptoms because they are unrelated to tizanidine
options.D: Blood-pressure effects occur only after treatment is stopped and are not relevant during titration

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed labeling identifies tizanidine as an alpha2-adrenergic agonist that can produce hypotension, with syncope reported postmarketing. Section 5.1 states that the risk of significant hypotension may be minimized by dose titration and by monitoring for signs and symptoms of hypotension before dosage increases; clients moving from a supine to an upright position may be at increased risk for orthostatic effects. B, C, and D directly contradict the label. The final item focuses on the exact safety teaching supported by the current warning rather than making a broader claim about continuous blood-pressure monitoring for every client in every setting.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current official tizanidine labeling directly supports hypotension and orthostatic-effect monitoring during titration, particularly before dosage increases.
candidate.source_locator: DailyMed current tizanidine labeling → Section 5.1 'Hypotension': tizanidine is an alpha2-adrenergic agonist that can produce hypotension; syncope has been reported; risk may be minimized by dose titration and monitoring for signs/symptoms of hypotension before dosage increase; moving from supine to upright may increase risk of hypotension and orthostatic effects.
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine (DailyMed; FDA-approved prescribing information)
candidate.source_version_date: Current DailyMed labeling available in 2026; current label accessed 2026-08-18
candidate.stem: A nurse is teaching a client who is starting tizanidine for spasticity. Which safety teaching is most important during dose titration?
